Lifecycle logic is duplicated against its own rule. event-lifecycle.ts says 'Single source of truth ... Do not re-derive this rule locally', yet generate-site.ts:245-257 re-derives the exhibition end_date rule inline for upcomingEvents.

Encoding is inconsistent end to end: titles are stored HTML-escaped in the DB ('«LONE»', 'Rising Road & Deuxcadance'). Each emitter decodes differently, so search-index and JSON-LD leak entities while cards do not.

Two slug algorithms are kept apart deliberately (event-page.ts:140-172). slugify drops Greek, so titles like 'ΤΖΟΝΙ ΜΠΛΕ 2ος Χρόνος' become '2e071062-anesis-2'. There are two sibling dirs per event ('7866dc83--4' and '7866dc83-theatro-chorn-4').

tsconfig include covers only src/** and tests/**, so the 102 scripts/*.ts, including the scrapers, are not type-checked. The package.json 'test' script points to scripts/test-pipeline.ts, which does not exist.

overall_notes: Strong engineering scaffolding (gates, tests, provenance, careful comments, an honest session log) sits around a product whose public facts and surface are weaker than the tooling suggests. The three biggest problems a user or answer engine would meet today are all on the live site as well as the local build. (1) Invented or phantom facts: venue-default prices shown as real on about 40% of listings and in schema offers.price, the Megaron 20:30 default on about 20%, and about 48 athinorama year-rollover phantoms. (2) Visible pipeline artefacts: a literal '<!-- timeliness-expires -->' on 662 pages, '[PLACEHOLDER]' on 6 hubs, raw markdown tables on 44 pages. (3) i18n breakage: English hubs render Greek cards, and Greek pages carry English descriptions, meta and addresses. Coverage is also thin: 429 listed events, 4 exhibitions, and 31% of the visible DB population hidden because an enrichment concern suppresses the whole event. Measurement, the INTENT focus #1, is mostly unbuilt: citations and crawlers are null, and there is no click telemetry. Performance and baseline accessibility are the healthiest areas. Not verified: whether ONX.Exhibition.NY.2026 actually shows in Athens (the Onassis page was not fetched), and whether Phantom Spell's '€22' or '€25/30' is the true price.
